_doc: The creature kit (scenes/art_pixel/creature_kit.gd, docs/rendering.md 'The creature kit'): creatures as parametric skeletons. 'kits' maps a kit name to its parameters (a kit may extend another with 'base'); a body part with 'kit': '<name>' is completed from it (sockets, anchors, cut legs, posed walk, idle poses, gait) and its head and legs are made. DataLib registers every kit here on load and completes the kit parts in data/parts.json: the bears (bear_brown, bear_black, bear_polar on two legs, bear_mount on four; in play since 2026-10-17, D-161). This file's own parts and creatures are staged only by tests and sheets (CreatureKit.stage): the alley cat (D-124) rebuilt through the kit, to compare with the game's hand-built cat: 'kitcat' keeps the cat's modelled body and head (big_cat.py) on the kit's skeleton, legs and sockets; 'kitcat_built' builds the body and head from the kit's own primitives too.

_params_doc.posture: quadruped (shoulder and hip joints on a spine) or biped (hips, a torso leaning `lean` degrees forward about them)
_params_doc.scale: the whole creature after it's built (part units)
_params_doc.fur, fur_units: the coat's texture and its tiling; colours are the skin palette: skin (fur), skin2 (dark: stripes, paws), skin3 (pale: muzzle, chest), skin4 (socks)
_params_doc.shoulder, hip: joint positions [x, y] (quadruped: fore and hind leg roots; biped: the pelvis)
_params_doc.leg_z: the legs' half spacing across the body
_params_doc.body: torso volumes {at, r, mat, rot} named chest, waist, rump, belly, pelvis, hump (upright for a biped), patches (markings), or mesh (+ drop) for a modelled torso over the same skeleton
_params_doc.neck: {from, to, r, into}: to is the head socket; into (a point in the head's frame, in the back of the skull) makes the neck one mass running into the head, the head held out of the body's bake so they join without a line (the bear mount, B3)
_params_doc.fore, hind (quadruped): bones (hind: femur, tibia, metatarsus; fore: humerus, forearm, pastern), r per bone [top, end], mats, paw size, x (the paw's rest place under the joint), tilt (the lowest bone from upright, degrees: a digitigrade hock about 18, a plantigrade sole about 75), walk_tilt [start, end of stance], swing_tilt, scapula (fore), claws
_params_doc.leg (biped): bones [thigh, shin], r, foot (length), heel (behind the ankle), ankle (height), foot_r, x
_params_doc.arm (biped): shoulder (upright, near side), elbow (from the shoulder), hand and hand_l (the near hand's rest, the shield hand), r per bone, paw; the near arm is the front layer, posed for the hold by unit_models.arm_pose
_params_doc.walk: stride, stance (share of the cycle a foot is down), lift, steps (baked per leg), phases (quadruped footfall order, x PI), toe_off (biped), gait (UnitView's cadence, bob, rock)
_params_doc.sit (quadruped): order (the idle poses, going down) and poses {pitch, hip_y, hind [x, tilt] or fold {hock, paw, out}, head [dx, dy] (the head raised on its neck)}, fore [x, tilt]
_params_doc.idle (biped): idle poses {forward, out, pitch} moving the feet only (the torso stays, so worn armour still fits)
_params_doc.head: skull, cheeks, stop, muzzle {from, to, r, bridge}, nose, eyes {look, r, iris}, brow, ears {shape round|point, at, size}, whiskers, bridle, top, gear_scale, k (its scale), tilt (degrees, nose up +); or mesh
_params_doc.head_of: take the head from another kit, changing only what this kit's head names (a mount carrying the biped's head pitched down)
_params_doc.tack: saddle (seat height over the back), cloth (a saddle cloth and girth for a mount)
_params_doc.sockets: overrides of what the skeleton derives (seat, girth, hand, torso, back, wings), and a biped's drape (a hero's cape or pelt) or a socket named for a part (cape.cloth), where it hangs clear of a broad back
_params_doc.stance: legs.stance for the placement check (relaxed per idle pose)

neck._doc: the neck runs into the back of the skull (the head-join rule: the head sat on a thin neck a notch below the withers' line)
B3 (D-126): a little shorter and thicker than B2's (to [3.0, 26.4], r [3.2, 2.6]), so it reads as a bear, not a long-necked animal

head._doc: B2: the biped's head (k keeps its size under the mount's scale 1.3), carried low and pitched nose-down

neck._doc: B3: one thick mass from the hump into the back of the skull (into: a point in the head's frame), as wide as the head, the top line hump -> neck -> crown without a notch (B2's short neck from [9, 17] to [13, 12.4], r [4, 3.4], left a step: 'broken neck')
